user_message: My estimate for the number of atoms in a 1 cm cube of water is 10^12. Don't just replace it: diagnose the likely missing scale, give one hint, and ask me to revise the estimate.
allowed_evidence: A cubic centimeter of water has a mass of about 1 gram. Water's molar mass is about 18 grams per mole, and one mole contains about 6 × 10^23 molecules. Each water molecule contains three atoms.
public_rubric: Identifies the missing mole-to-particle scale without stating the completed atom count.
Provides exactly one actionable quantitative hint.
Invites the learner to recompute a power-of-ten estimate while keeping units visible.
